territorial_scope.description: US export rules applied to named entities in China, Japan, Singapore and South Korea, with footnote 5 entities also subject to foreign-produced items under § 734.9(e)(3).

evidence.quote: includes foreign-produced items that are subject to the EAR under § 734.9(e)(3) of the EAR

summary.short: Final rule adding 140 entities to the US Entity List (China, Japan, Singapore, South Korea), modifying 14 existing entries, and removing three entities from the Validated End-User program. Listed parties face export license requirements, generally with a presumption of denial, effective 2 December 2024.
summary.long: The rule amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to add 140 entities to the Entity List, under China, Japan, Singapore and South Korea, and to modify 14 existing China entries. Listed entities face a license requirement for all items subject to the EAR, generally with a presumption of denial. Nine added entries and seven modified entries carry a Footnote 5 designation, which also covers foreign-produced items subject to the EAR under § 734.9(e)(3). Wuhan Xinxin Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited is eligible for License Exception RFF. The rule removes CSMC Technologies Corporation, Shanghai Huahong Grace Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation and Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment, Inc., China from the Validated End-User program (supplement no. 7 to part 748). Shipments en route may proceed under prior eligibility until January 2, 2025 (January 31, 2025 for Footnote 5-related changes). The rule is effective December 2, 2024; Footnote 5-related Entity List requirements have a compliance date of December 31, 2024. Authority cited is Export Control Reform Act of 2018 sections 1753 and 1754. BIS estimates 200 additional annual license applications.

The entity list is a selection of named entities from the rule's amendments; the full set of 140 added entities and 14 modified entries appears in the Supplement No. 4 amendments and table. Internal inconsistency: Part II.A narrative says the ERC 'determined to add the following 106 entities', while the list adds 140 entities across destinations. LEI and ticker values are not stated in the text and are left empty. Entity-level license requirements and presumptions of denial are as stated in the rule's table; the Footnote 5 entries rely on the concurrent FDP interim final rule.

enforcement.note: The rule adds entities to the Entity List with license requirements and presumption-of-denial review policy, but states no fine, penalty, criminal sanction, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking for violating them. It cites ECRA (50 U.S.C. 4801–4852) as legal basis only. The Paperwork Reduction Act paragraph says no person is subject to a penalty for failing to respond to a collection of information without a valid OMB control number; this is not a sanction regime for the listed conduct.
